rationale: Both candidates correctly validate the core orchestrator fix (removing the already_submitted gate is safe because both submit_initial and submit_update reject list prompts), matching the sole ground-truth inline comment — Y articulates this slightly more precisely than X. But Y's review pivots on a sweeping 'blocker' claim (sections 2/2a/2b) that ZImagePipeline.forward's signature was silently reduced by an unrelated prior PR, making the Ming pipeline call in this diff throw TypeError on every invocation — a claim built on unverifiable external commit history (specific SHAs for a separate PR) rather than the diff itself, and flatly contradicted by the actual outcome (two clean LGTM approvals, no such issue raised). That fabricated-risk claim drives Y's 'Request changes' verdict, which is a serious grounding failure since it's the headline of the review. X stays tightly grounded in the diff, correctly validates both changes as resolved/correct, and only raises hedged, appropriately-scoped nits (missing test coverage, unrelated CI gate check) without overreaching.
